NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday raised questions over changes made to Form 6, the application used for registering a voter, during the Election Commission 's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The issue came up while the court was hearing petitions alleging that several decisions linked to the SIR exercise were taken without the approval of all three election commissioners, particularly Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, who were at odds with poll body chief Gyanesh Kumar on multiple occasions.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana sought responses from the Election Commission, the Centre, the CEC and the other two election commissioners before examining whether the poll panel's statutory procedure was followed.The bench, however, refused to pass an immediate order seeking the suspension of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, while considering the controversy over Form 6, which was one of the central issues raised in the petitions.Form 6 is the application through which an eligible person seeks inclusion of their name in the electoral roll. The Election Commission's guidelines states the application is addressed to the Electoral Registration Officer of the constituency where the applicant ordinarily resides.The form requires basic details such as the applicant's name, details of a relative, Aadhaar information, gender, date of birth and present ordinary residence. Applicants are also required to complete a declaration, with the guidelines warning that making a false statement in it is punishable under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.The Election Commission's instructions also mandates that an applicant can fill the form either in English or in the official language of the state. Also, an applicant who does not know the number or name of the relevant constituency cannot have the application rejected merely for that reason.For age verification, applicants can submit a self-attested copy of one of the documents specified in the form. The guidelines also provide for verification by the Electoral Registration Officer in cases where the prescribed documents are unavailable.The petitions allege that additional requirements connected with the SIR were introduced into Form 6 through the Election Commission's software.One of the allegations is that details concerning an applicant's ancestry (details of father or grandfather) and a link to the previous SIR were incorporated into the process without an amendment to the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.The petitioners have further alleged that Election Commissioner Vivek Joshi objected to the modification and that Election Commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu subsequently endorsed the objection. Therefore, the issue therefore goes beyond the information sought from voters.At the heart of the dispute is whether the Election Commission could alter the form and introduce SIR-linked requirements through its software without following the legal process required for changing the relevant electoral rules. During the hearing, the CJI specifically flagged the question of who authorised the modification.“Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let's be clear. When record has produced, we would like to see who has modified. But, your prayers appear jumbled up,” the CJI noted, as quoted by LiveLaw.The court, however, did not accept the petitioners' allegations as established facts at this stage as Justice Bagchi said the court would first need responses from the concerned authorities and records before deciding whether any decision was taken contrary to the statutory framework."If records show some decision was not unanimous etc., we will injunct those decisions and say they are ultra-vires. Can we ex-parte come to decision that all decisions were unilateral? We expect them to respond in a clear, transparent manner," Justice Bagchi added.Amid the raging controvery, the Election Commission withdrew the additional SIR-related declaration from Form 6 in states where the electoral roll revision exercise had been completed.In states where the SIR was concluded, the EC removed additional declaration from the ECINET app and portal, as well as the respective Chief Electoral Officer portals. This meant that applicants in states where SIR is over will only need to fill the regular statutory Form 6 to enrol as voters.Just days before this action and as the controvery over dissent in the poll body emerged, the EC in a press note had, however, said that "the declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon’ble Supreme Court. For non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used."The Form 6 dispute forms part of a broader challenge to how the Election Commission has allegedly handled the SIR exercise. The petitions rely on claims that the two other Election Commissioners formally raised objections on at least 14 occasions over several months to decisions and orders concerning the revision of electoral rolls.The allegations include changes to electoral-roll software, communications issued in the name of the Election Commission and other decisions allegedly taken without the approval of all members of the multi-member poll panel.The petitioners have invoked Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023. The provision states that the Commission's business should, as far as possible, be transacted unanimously and that where the members differ, the matter is to be decided according to the majority view.The pleas argue that this framework means powers vested in the Election Commission cannot be exercised individually by the CEC where the law requires the Commission to act collectively.The petitioners have sought several forms of relief, including suspension of Gyanesh Kumar as CEC until the matter is decided, preservation of electoral-roll data and audit trails, and restrictions on further substantive changes to Form 6.Another plea has sought criminal proceedings against the CEC and other officials and argued that decisions, guidelines and software changes allegedly made without the full Commission's agreement should be declared unconstitutional, ultra vires and void ab initio.The Supreme Court has therefore, at this stage, not ruled on whether the alleged changes to Form 6 or other SIR-related decisions were unlawful. The immediate question before the court is whether the Election Commission followed the statutory decision-making process.The court will consider the records and responses of the respondents before deciding whether any particular decision can be struck down.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Monday raised questions over changes made to Form 6, the application used for registering a voter, during the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The issue came up while the court was hearing petitions alleging that several decisions linked to the SIR were taken without the approval of all three election commissioners.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday stressed the need for stronger measures to prevent crimes against women in Delhi, saying authorities must create an environment where women feel safe while walking on the streets or travelling by public transport.A bench led by Justice JB Pardiwala was hearing a suo motu case initiated by the court over recent rape cases and other crimes against women in Delhi-NCR."There appears to be a feeling that women are not safe in city particularly in some vulnerable pockets," the court observed, flagging concerns over the safety of women in certain parts of the national capital.The bench told the Centre and Delhi Police that the focus should be on preventing crimes rather than dealing with them after they have occurred."We must ensure every woman in NCT Delhi feels safe, whether walking at 10 PM or travelling by metro or road," the court said.The Supreme Court also said deficiencies in the system should not create conditions that allow crimes to take place."Deficiencies, if any, should not facilitate commission of crime," the court said."What is important is to prevent crime, not what you do after crime is committed," it observed.The court also stressed the need to create a strong deterrent for those who may be inclined to commit such offences.“Unless you don’t create such fright in the minds if the criminals ki ab kuch kiya toh mar jayengey (if we commit such a crime we will die) you will not be able to prevent such crimes”, Justice JB Pardiwala said.“You need to create a fright, a fear in the mind of a man who is prone to commit such officers”, the judge said.The Supreme Court told Delhi Police that it should take a firm approach against those accused of committing serious crimes against women, while also referring to concerns that could be raised under Article 21, which guarantees the right to life and personal liberty.The court said authorities should not be deterred from taking strict action against those accused of rape and other serious offences because of criticism from human rights groups.
Article Summary: Supreme Court says authorities must create an environment where women feel safe while walking on the streets or travelling by public transport. A bench led by Justice JB Pardiwala was hearing a suo motu case initiated by the court over recent rape cases.

NEW DELHI: A political row erupted between the Congress and members of NDA after a video showing a brief interruption during Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman's speech in Andhra Pradesh's Madanapalle on October 2 went viral on social media.The 30-second clip showed Andhra Pradesh chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu addressing the crowd during Sitharaman's speech. A social media user claimed that people in the gathering were demanding jobs. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh later reposted the clip and alleged that the crowd's reaction reflected public anger."The finance minister herself is seeing how much anger there is among the public. The chief minister had to silence the people," Ramesh said.Sitharaman rejected the Congress leader's interpretation, saying workers of the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) and Jana Sena Party were eager to meet their leaders, Naidu and Pawan Kalyan, during the event.Calling Ramesh's conclusion "unbelievable", Sitharaman said Naidu had only asked the workers to wait until the programme ended before interacting with the leaders."Unbelievable, Jairam. Didn't think you were impetuous. The workers of both TDP and Jana Sena Party wanted to meet their leaders, Chandrababu Naidu and Pawan Kalyan.The chief minister only said they would meet them after the programme ended. That was all," Sitharaman said in the comment section of Ramesh's post.Naidu also hit back at Ramesh, saying the clip had been presented as evidence of public anger when the gathering had actually witnessed an enthusiastic response."Jairam ji, your interpretation of what happened could not be further from reality. What you are trying to falsely portray as public anger was, in fact, an overwhelming and enthusiastic response from the people. The sheer enthusiasm of the gathering required me to intervene briefly so that the programme could continue smoothly," Naidu said.State minister Nara Lokesh, who was present at the event, also criticised Ramesh, accusing him of promoting a false narrative without verifying the circumstances.Lokesh said there had been no protest among the crowd and alleged that a routine interaction with an enthusiastic gathering had been selectively presented to suggest public discontent.
Article Summary: A video showing a brief interruption during Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman's speech in Andhra Pradesh's Madanapalle on October 2 went viral on social media. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh later reposted the clip and alleged that the crowd's reaction reflected public anger.

Article Title: Delhi riots: HC rejects pleas seeking FIR against political leaders over 'hate speeches'
Article Text:
HC rejected pleas seeking registration of FIRs.

NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Monday dismissed a batch of petitions seeking an SIT probe into the 2020 Delhi riotsand the violence at Jamia Millia Islamia during anti-CAA protests in December 2019.A bench of Justices Vivek Chaudhary and Manoj Jain said, “for the reasons mentioned in the judgment, all the petitions are dismissed”.“The batch is decided into two parts, one is northeast Delhi riots and another is for Jamia Millia riots,” the bench said while pronouncing the verdict, PTI reported.The court also rejected pleas seeking registration of FIRs against political leaders over alleged “hate speeches” linked to the 2020 riots and action against police officers accused of dereliction of duty. The court had reserved its verdict on the petitions on July 24.In the northeast Delhi riots matter, the petitions sought directions for setting up an SIT, a commission of inquiry or a fact-finding committee to examine various aspects of the violence.The pleas also sought medical treatment and compensation for those affected, besides registration of FIRs against police officers accused of lapses. Some petitioners also sought FIRs against political leaders over alleged hate speeches.A communal clash broke out in northeast Delhi on February 24, 2020, amid protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act. At least 53 people were killed and around 700 injured in the violence.Shaikh Mujtaba sought FIRs against BJP leaders Kapil Mishra, Anurag Thakur, Parvesh Verma and Abhay Verma over their speeches.Lawyers Voice sought FIRs over alleged hate speeches by several leaders, including Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Manish Sisodia, Amanatullah Khan, Akbaruddin Owaisi and Waris Pathan.CPI(M) leader Brinda Karat sought an independent probe into alleged excesses by police, Rapid Action Force personnel and other officials.Another petitioner, Ajay Gautam, sought an NIA probe into the alleged funding of anti-CAA protests, along with FIRs against political leaders over alleged inflammatory speeches, ANI reported.The Supreme Court had earlier asked the high court to decide one of the pleas expeditiously. The other petitions concerned violence at Jamia Millia Islamia during anti-CAA protests in December 2019.Students alleged that police assaulted them during the protests and sought an independent probe into the alleged police action. In some petitions, the petitioners also sought transfer of the investigation from the Delhi Police to an outside agency.One petitioner, Nabila Hasan, who was then a law student, had also approached the National Human Rights Commission.The Delhi Police opposed the pleas, saying it had collected and preserved CCTV footage from cameras inside and outside the university and in the New Friends Colony area. It also argued that transferring the investigation would unnecessarily widen the scope of the proceedings.
Article Summary: HC rejected pleas seeking registration of FIRs. At least 53 people were killed and around 700 injured in the violence. The Delhi Police opposed the pleas, saying it had collected and preserved CCTV footage from cameras inside and outside the university and in the New Friends Colony area.

Article Title: Beyond advocacy: Government steps up diplomatic push for Ukraine settlement
Article Text:

External affairs minister S Jaishankar said Sunday India's approach to the Russia-Ukraine war had moved beyond just the advocacy of dialogue and diplomacy between the 2 countries, suggesting India might be looking to actively mediate in the conflict. Both Moscow and Kyiv have said in the past few days that India had come up with ideas and proposals to bring the war to an end.Unlike China and other countries that have looked to mediate, India had so far offered support for all global peace initiatives - advocating engagement between the involved parties - but without introducing any signature proposal. This approach was anchored in its own emphasis on bilateralism in resolving disputes between countries.Offering a teaser about India's proposal, Jaishankar said India is looking to address some immediate concerns that both Russia and Ukraine have on "grain exports, energy exports, non-attack possibilities"."We would like to see an end to this conflict. This will require dialogue and diplomacy. We have been advocating it for many years, and in recent months we have got a little bit more involved beyond advocacy. We have conversations with both Russia and Ukraine in this regard.We are trying to be helpful, starting with the Black Sea safety of shipping issue," said the minister, speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting here.Jaishankar had himself said during his visit to Ukraine last month – shortly after PM Narendra Modi's message to President Vladimir to stop the "endless war – that India was discussing ideas that could be developed for cessation of hostilities. On Friday, while Putin had announced Modi had very good ideas for peace, Ukraine foreign minister Andrii Sybiha said India had come up with the "broadest" peace proposal out of the 4 that it had received from other countries, including the US.This shift in India's position seems driven by the direct domestic fallout of the conflict, whether it's commercial shipping disruptions in the Black Sea or an intense blowback from the US over India's continued purchase of Russian crude.In his remarks – not for the first time – Jaishankar stressed that Russia had stood by India when the latter’s security and territorial integrity was threatened and that India’s current approach to Moscow is shaped by the legacy.“At a time when much of the world preferred backing a military regime next to us (Pakistan), Russia was a country with which our relations were very good, and we are shaped in many ways by that legacy,” he said.On the US, Jaishankar said that the world today was marked by a radical repositioning of the US which had deliberately chosen to become a "lonelier power" and also the rise of China.“The current system was significantly underwritten by the United States. That underwriting is diluting. There are gaps which have emerged,” he said.The minister underlined that the sharp competition between the US and China was not limited to these 2 countries alone. "It has led to weaponization of any leverage that any country has. And that competition coexists with the complexity of interdependence," said the minister.
Article Summary: India's external affairs minister S Jaishankar said Sunday India's approach to the Russia-Ukraine war had moved beyond just the advocacy of dialogue and diplomacy. He suggested India might be looking to actively mediate in the conflict. Both Moscow and Kyiv have said in the past few days that India had come up with ideas to bring the war to an end.

Article Title: Ex-Army jawan among 2 held for 'passing' information to Pak on defence movements: Assam CM
Article Text:
Two held in Assam over alleged Pakistan links

NEW DELHI: Two people, including a retired Army jawan who was later re-employed on a contractual basis, were arrested in Assam for allegedly sharing security-related information with Pakistan, chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said on Sunday.Sarma said the arrests were made by Assam Police based on inputs from central agencies. “Today, as per input of central agencies, the Assam Police arrested two persons. One is a retired army jawan but currently working on a contractual basis with the army,” he said at a press conference.“It has been alleged that they were in touch with Pakistan and were giving information about army movement. We will hand them over to the central agencies,” news agency PTI quoted Sarma saying.The chief minister said initial reports suggested the two suspects were allegedly honey-trapped by individuals seeking to obtain information from them.Earlier, Assam Police said its special task force had arrested 31-year-old Abhishek Kumar Singh, a Bihar native living in Guwahati, for alleged espionage activities. Singh, who is from Purba Champaran, was suspected of sharing sensitive information about security forces with a Pakistani intelligence operative (PIO).Police said the initial input about Singh came from Military Intelligence of the Tezpur-based Gajraj Corps. The STF, in coordination with Sonitpur Police, subsequently gathered information on his alleged activities and links with the PIO.Singh was apprehended from his rented accommodation in Guwahati during an operation conducted in the intervening night of October 3 and 4, police said. A mobile phone, SIM cards and documents described as incriminating were recovered from him.“Further investigation is underway,” the police statement said.
Article Summary: Two people arrested in Assam for allegedly sharing security-related information with Pakistan. Chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said the arrests were made by Assam Police based on inputs from central agencies. One of the suspects is a retired army jawan who was later re-employed on a contractual basis.

Article Title: Monthly stipend for senior, junior resident doctors to increase from Rs 75,000 to Rs 1 lakh: Uttarakhand CM
Article Text:
Monthly stipend for senior, junior resident doctors to increase from Rs 75,000 to Rs 1 lakh: Uttarakhand CM Dhami

Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Sunday announced that stipends for both Senior and Junior Resident doctors in the state have been raised significantly from approximately Rs 75,000 to over Rs 1 lakh per month.Speaking to the media after the State cabinet meeting in Banbasa, CM Dhami added that around 25-26 decisions were taken during the meeting.He noted that the deadline for regularising 'Class B' lands in key regions, including Dehradun, Lalkuan, and Bindukhatta, has been extended by one year."We have increased the stipends for our Senior and Junior Resident doctors; the amount, which was previously around Rs 75,000, has now been raised to over Rs 1 lakh. Additionally, we have extended the deadline by one year for the regularisation of 'Class B' lands in areas like Dehradun, Lalkuan, and Bindukhatta. Many other decisions have also been taken, particularly concerning these border regions, totalling around twenty-five or twenty-six decisions," he said.He added that the Cabinet thoroughly deliberated on managing major state events and seasonal pilgrim traffic.According to the chief minister, the Cabinet held discussions on ensuring smooth operations, strict travel management, and maintaining optimal road conditions across pilgrim routes amid the ongoing Char Dham Yatra."The Char Dham Yatra is currently underway, and we discussed ensuring its smooth management and proper arrangements, including maintaining good road conditions," he said.He added, "We also deliberated on managing the traffic flow at Kainchi Dham, where the volume of visitors has surged significantly. Furthermore, we discussed the ongoing 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan."He emphasised that Prime Minister Narendra Modi completed 25 years of governance on October 7th and programs across all districts will be held to mark the occassion.Furthermore, the chief minister underlined that the State government is putting efforts in the region based on the vision of an 'Adarsh ​​Champawat' (Model Champawat), with all the departments working cohesively here."We have initiated efforts to ensure the government reaches even the remote border areas. This region, comprising Banbasa and Tanakpur, falls under the Champawat district, where work is progressing based on the vision of an 'Adarsh ​​Champawat' (Model Champawat). All departments are actively working here; the entire Cabinet, along with officials from various departments, has arrived today. This will undoubtedly provide fresh momentum to the region's development and inspire the local people," he said.Highlighting the military cantonment and BSF deployment, CM Dhami said that the region shares a neighbourly relationship with Nepal, with similar attire, culture, and modes of worship. So, the government has initiated the practice of reaching out to the people before taking major State-level decisions."There is a military cantonment here, and a large number of Border Security Force (BSF) personnel are deployed in the area. This is a region bordering Nepal, and we share deep, age-old ties, often described as 'roti-beti' (bonds of food and kinship/marriage) with our neighbours there. The culture across this region is uniform, and the modes of worship are similar; consequently, the government has initiated a practice of reaching out directly to the people to make major state-level decisions. We will continue to take significant decisions in the future," he remarked.Notably, this marks the first time a State cabinet meeting is being held outside the capital city of Dehradun, in Banbasa along the Indo-Nepal border.
Article Summary: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Sunday announced that stipends for both Senior and Junior Resident doctors in the state have been raised from approximately Rs 75,000 to over Rs 1 lakh per month. The deadline for regularising 'Class B' lands in key regions, including Dehradun, Lalkuan, and Bindukhatta, has also been extended.

Article Title: CM Pushkar Singh Dhami chairs first-ever cabinet meeting in Champawat to boost border area development
Article Text:
CM Pushkar Singh Dhami chairs first-ever cabinet meeting in Champawat to boost border area development

BANBASA: In a new initiative aimed at taking governance to the remote and border areas of Uttarakhand, chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami chaired a state cabinet meeting at the NHPC complex in Banbasa, Champawat district, bordering the India-Nepal international border.This was the first-ever cabinet meeting held in Champawat district, during which several important decisions were taken.Chief minister Dhami said Cabinet meetings would no longer remain confined to Dehradun and would also be held in different districts across the state. This would provide an opportunity to place local issues, development potential and regional priorities directly before the government. He said the state government was working to reduce the gap between governance and the people and ensure that the benefits of development schemes reach the last mile.The chief minister said border areas were not merely the geographical boundaries of the state but also an important link in the country's security, culture and development. He said connecting people living in border areas with the mainstream of development was a priority of the state government. Infrastructure, employment, tourism and connectivity in these areas were being further strengthened.He said holding cabinet meetings in different parts of the state would help the government understand local conditions, public expectations and development needs more closely.It would also pave the way for effective and prompt decisions on issues specific to particular regions.During the cabinet meeting in Banbasa, chief minister Dhami and members of his council of ministers were presented with the traditional Farra/Chhantoli, an invaluable symbol of Uttarakhand's rich folk traditions. The traditional shield is associated with the famous Bagwal tradition of Devidhura in Champawat.The traditional shield used during the Bagwal tradition is primarily made from bamboo or ringal strips and crafted in an umbrella-like shape. Presenting the traditional Farra/Chhantoli to the CM and cabinet ministers served as a symbol of respect for the folk culture, traditions and distinctive cultural identity of the state's border region.
Article Summary: Chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said Cabinet meetings would no longer remain confined to Dehradun. This would provide an opportunity to place local issues, development potential and regional priorities directly before the government. Infrastructure, employment, tourism and connectivity in these areas were being further strengthened.

NEW DELHI: Protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar intensified in Delhi on Sunday, with AAP workers, AISA and NSUI activists among those detained as demonstrators attempted to march towards Jantar Mantar for the third consecutive day.AAP workers, members of its student wing ASAP, NSUI workers, AISA activists and members of other organisations took part in the demonstrations, prompting heavy deployment of Delhi Police and paramilitary personnel across central Delhi.The protests are part of a wider agitation over alleged irregularities in the Election Commission’s functioning, the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and alleged mass deletion of voters.AISA members and activists from several organisations marched from the Ashoka Road area towards Jantar Mantar but were stopped by police barricades.The protesters briefly clashed with security personnel as they tried to cross the barricades. AISA national president Neha Bora was among those seen attempting to breach the police cordon. Senior advocates Prashant Bhushan and Kapil Sibal also participated in the protest.The mobilisation began from Andhra Bhawan Circle on Ashoka Road, with protesters raising slogans against Kumar and demanding his resignation.AISA members later alleged that Bora was taken away in a private vehicle and that her whereabouts were initially unknown.The organisation said the detention took place as its activists attempted to return to Jantar Mantar for the third consecutive day despite heavy barricading and security arrangements.Visuals showed Bora attempting to climb over a barricade as police officials tried to stop her.Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke slammed Delhi Police for detaining Bora, saying it has “once again shown cowardice”.In a post on X, Dipke said, “Delhi Police has once again shown its cowardice by detaining Neha and Rosy for simply raising their voices. Rosy yesterday was molested by ACP Vivek Bhagat and instead of acting against the pervert, the cops detained her.“So much for women empowerment Narendra Modi,” he added.More than a dozen AAP workers were detained during the protest at India Gate, including Delhi unit chief Saurabh Bharadwaj and MLA Sanjeev Jha.Visuals from the protest showed AAP workers blocking buses carrying detained protesters as security personnel tried to clear the area. The situation escalated when protesters broke through barricades and moved towards Jantar Mantar, where Delhi Police and the Rapid Action Force were deployed to stop them.Bharadwaj alleged that police manhandled him during the detention and said protesters were being treated harshly.“They are picking me up and throwing me around like I am a football... There is such a large police force here, yet they are not even registering an FIR against their own ACP, nor are they arresting the ACP,” he said.Bharadwaj also shared a photograph on X, saying he had been turned upside down by Delhi Police at India Gate to hide his face from cameras.“These are my shoes in the air,” he said.AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal criticised the police action on X, saying, “This is absolutely shocking. Modi ji has left even Hitler behind.”The protests have also triggered a controversy over allegations of sexual harassment and misconduct by police personnel during Saturday’s demonstrations.Three women identifying themselves as journalists complained that they were manhandled and sexually harassed by police officers while covering the protests near Jantar Mantar on October 3.Delhi Police said the complaints had been received, medical examinations conducted and the matter transferred to the Crime Branch for a “fair and impartial enquiry”.CPM leader Brinda Karat criticised the police over the handling of the complaints and questioned the reported demand for video evidence before registering an FIR.“Now, when sexual harassment is happening with a journalist and Delhi Police is trying to save him and it is being asked to show the video,” Karat said, calling the response “extremely wrong”.Opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi, have also criticised the alleged police conduct and demanded accountability.More than 500 protesters, including student activists and political leaders, were detained during demonstrations in central Delhi on Friday. AAP leaders, Bora and activist Yogendra Yadav were among those detained.Police had denied permission for Friday’s gathering and deployed additional personnel across central Delhi. Several roads leading towards Jantar Mantar were barricaded, while access to some metro stations in the area was temporarily restricted during the earlier protests.This comes after a report in The Indian Express said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally raised objections on at least 14 occasions over 10 months regarding decisions concerning electoral rolls, voter registration and the Commission’s technology systems.The Election Commission, however, rejected the suggestion that the reported objections amounted to institutional dissent over final decisions.The poll panel said operational queries, inputs and suggestions raised during the draft stage were part of its standard administrative and decision-making process. The ECI also said decisions regarding the schedule of the SIR exercise were unanimous.
Article Summary: Protests demand resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Demonstrators attempted to march towards Jantar Mantar for third consecutive day. AISA national president Neha Bora was among those seen attempting to breach the police cordon.

Article Title: 'Russia stood by us when our territorial integrity was under threat': Jaishankar

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Sunday highlighted India's longstanding ties with Russia, saying the country had stood by us when New Delhi's security and territorial integrity faced threats and much of the world preferred backing a military regime.Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, Jaishankar said India and Russia had maintained strong relations since the 1950s and that the legacy of those ties continued to shape the relationship.“India and Russia have historically very good relations, particularly since the 1950s. That history is not forgotten,” Jaishankar said.He added that Russia which was Soviet Union before “stood by us in many ways when our security, when our territorial integrity was under threat”.“At a time when much of the world preferred backing a military regime (Pakistan) next to us, Russia was a country with which our relations were very good, and we are shaped in many ways by that legacy,” he said.“Today, the relationship has widened beyond that... It is very much more today an economic relationship as well. So there is a military component, there are nuclear component, there is space issues, but there is a significant amount of trade and investment between the two countries and energy and resources as well...India's experience has been quite positive and consistently positive” he added.Jaishankar also said India had moved beyond simply advocating dialogue and diplomacy to taking a more active role in efforts to resolve the Ukraine conflict.He said India had held conversations with both Kyiv and Moscow in recent months and was trying to address some immediate concerns arising from the conflict.“Our position on that conflict has been very clear, which is that we would like to see an end to this conflict. This will require dialogue and diplomacy. There has to be negotiations in this regard,” he said.“We have been advocating it for many years, and in recent months we have got a little bit more involved beyond advocacy. We have conversations with both Russia and Ukraine in this regard. We are trying to be helpful, starting with the Black Sea safety of shipping issue,” he added.Jaishankar said India's efforts were focused initially on ensuring the safety of shipping in the Black Sea, while also addressing issues related to grain and energy exports.“India is going beyond that to cover some immediate concerns which both of them (Russia and Ukraine) have on grain exports, energy exports, non-attack possibilities. Those are ongoing conversations right now,” he said.His remarks came days after Russian President Vladimir Putin said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had “good ideas” for finding a mutually acceptable solution to the conflict.Ukraine foreign minister Andrii Sybiha had also said on Friday that Kyiv received separate proposals from India and three other countries on a possible ceasefire. India has for more than four years maintained that the Ukraine conflict should be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy, PTI reported.PM Modi held wide-ranging talks with Putin in Bishkek on August 31. During the meeting, the Prime Minister stated that “endless war must now give way to end of war”.
Article Summary: Jaishankar said India and Russia had maintained strong relations since the 1950s. He said India had moved beyond advocating dialogue and diplomacy to taking a more active role in efforts to resolve the Ukraine conflict. His remarks came days after Russian President Vladimir Putin said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had “good ideas” for finding a mutually acceptable solution to the conflict.

Article Title: Huge fireball erupts as Russian drone hits Kyiv bridge in daylight- video

A Russian drone struck Kyiv’s Northern Bridge on Sunday, with video showing a huge fireball erupting on the key Dnipro crossing as vehicles continued to travel across it.Two people were injured in the strike, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said, CNN reported.The strike came as German chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in Kyiv amid air raid sirens, explosions and the activation of air defence systems. Merz travelled to the Ukrainian capital alongside German economic affairs and energy minister Katarina Reiche to meet President Volodymyr Zelenskyy amid Russia’s escalating attacks on the city.“Ukraine needs all our support in the coming weeks,” Merz said, warning that if Russia is not stopped, its war machine could eventually turn against Europe.Video footage showed the moment the Northern Bridge was hit, sending a huge plume of fire and black smoke into the sky while cars were still moving across the bridge.It was the second time the Northern Bridge had been hit in as many days. Earlier, Kyiv’s Southern Bridge, which carries road traffic and the city’s subway system, was struck five times in less than 24 hours.Ukrainian officials have warned that repeated attacks on bridges could disrupt vital transport links across the Dnipro River and effectively divide the capital.Kyiv is split by the river, with government institutions and businesses largely on the right bank and predominantly residential areas on the left bank.Ukraine’s infrastructure minister said Sunday that Kyiv plans to build several alternative crossings over the Dnipro if attacks on the bridges continue.The latest Russian threat came after Zelenskyy said Ukraine would step up attacks on Russian oil refineries in response to Moscow’s strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.
Article Summary: Russian drone strikes Kyiv's Northern Bridge on Sunday. Video shows huge fireball erupting on the key Dnipro crossing. Two people were injured in the strike, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. German chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in Kyiv amid air raid sirens, explosions and activation of air defence systems.

Article Title: Flydubai flight incident: Omani co-pilot may have tried to cut fuel supply to engines after cockpit attack
Article Text:
Hamam al-Hammami, the accused co-pilot in the flydubai incident (Image source: LinkedIn)

Also read:

Report raises possibility engines were shut down

Emergency codes changed during crisis

Smit Machchhar recalls his fight to open cockpit door

Security questions emerge after attack

Investigation into co-pilot's background

The Omani co-pilot who attacked the captain of a flydubai flight bound for Tel Aviv may have tried to crash the aircraft in the Saudi desert after realising that passengers were about to thwart his attempt to seize control of the plane, according to an investigation by Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera cited by Ynet News.The report said the co-pilot, identified as Hamam al-Hammami, after repeatedly striking Indian captain Smit Machchhar with a crash axe, took control of the Boeing 737 after the injured captain activated the switch that allowed the cockpit door to be opened.Once he realised his plan to crash the aircraft would fail, he allegedly tried to bring it down in the Saudi desert.According to the investigation, the attacker disconnected the autopilot and pushed the aircraft's controls sharply forward, sending the plane into a steep descent. The aircraft lost around 16,000 feet in less than a minute.The Corriere della Sera investigation also raised a possibility not previously reported, that the co-pilot may have cut the fuel supply to the aircraft's engines.Two Boeing 737 captains who examined videos recorded inside the aircraft reached this possibility after noticing that the emergency lights in the passenger cabin suddenly came on during the flight, Ynet News reported.The emergency lighting is designed to assist passengers during an evacuation or when an aircraft is on the ground. According to the report, such lights would not normally be activated at cruising altitude.The two captains told Corriere della Sera that emergency lights can switch on when a Boeing 737 loses its main electrical power supply and moves to battery power. That can happen if the aircraft's generators or engines are shut down.Investigators will therefore need to establish whether the co-pilot moved the switches controlling fuel flow to the engines from the “Run” position to “Cutoff”, according to the report.Corriere della Sera said its investigation was based on passenger testimony, reports submitted to security authorities by the flight crew, accounts from people familiar with the incident, airport employees, air traffic controllers and data from several platforms.Videos recorded during the flight were analysed by Boeing 737 captains who spoke to the newspaper.The report also disclosed details about the emergency codes transmitted from the aircraft after additional pilots were called into the cockpit.One of the pilots transmitted squawk code 7700, which indicates a general emergency on a commercial aircraft without specifying its nature. Air traffic controllers initially did not understand what was happening.Seven minutes later, the aircraft's code was changed to 7500, the code indicating a suspected hijacking.By that point, the aircraft was approaching Jordanian airspace, and air traffic controllers instructed it to turn back. Seven minutes later, controllers directed the aircraft to continue to Tabuk in Saudi Arabia for an emergency landing.The flight, FZ1073, was travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv when the co-pilot attacked the captain with an emergency crash axe and attempted to take control of the aircraft.UAE authorities described the incident as a “terrorist attack”.The aircraft plunged around 16,000 feet in about 30 seconds before being levelled out after passengers overpowered the co-pilot.Aviation instructor Alberto Paduanelli, who recreated the descent in a flight simulator for Reuters, said the experience would have felt like a “vertical roller coaster” for those on board.Also read: The other side of September 30: How a family waited anxiously to see thier injured son Captain Smit Machchhar Indian captain Smit Machchhar has described how he fought to open the cockpit door while injured after the co-pilot attacked him, saying he realised the aircraft was going down and he had to act.“It began as a normal flight. The co-pilot wanted to pray, which a lot of locals do and which is not out of the ordinary,” Machchhar told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday. He said the co-pilot then suddenly struck him repeatedly on the back of his head.Machchhar said his vision became blurred and he eventually found himself lying on the cockpit floor as the aircraft descended sharply. “I had that one last fight left in me. Call it personal or call it for the people, but I thought that if I don't do it, I am going to die,” he said.He then pushed himself towards the cockpit door and managed to open it, allowing people outside to rush in and overpower the co-pilot. Machchhar said the door could be opened from inside using a twist knob, while those outside were trying unsuccessfully to enter using a code.Speaking to Prime Minister Narendra Modi from his hospital bed in Abu Dhabi on Friday, Machchhar said, “I was fighting for my life, but I was determined not to let others die.”The incident has also prompted questions about how the Omani co-pilot was able to board the flight and operate it despite concerns about his background.UAE authorities had shared a list of passengers and crew, including their nationalities, with Israel before the flight. Israeli officials said no passenger or crew member had triggered a security warning.Netanyahu subsequently instructed the head of the National Security Council to appoint an examiner to review “all security aspects regarding foreign civil aviation to Israel”.Authorities had already said the Omani co-pilot had been barred from flying by his own country because of concerns over his extremist views.The Shin Bet said Israel's transportation ministry was responsible for vetting passenger lists from foreign flights. Transportation minister Miri Regev said on X that security agencies were responsible for flight security and that her ministry had not received a passenger list or any warnings.Sharing passenger lists is standard aviation procedure. Dvir Rubenstien, head of aviation security at Israel's transportation ministry, told Army Radio that the ministry relies on security checks conducted locally and does not have the tools or ability to check every passenger on every flight.The co-pilot's background is also being examined.Royal Air Maroc told Reuters that he underwent three months of training with the airline in 2025, but his subsequent application to work there was rejected.Buckinghamshire New University in Britain said he had completed a distance-learning course in aviation management, but not pilot training.An Australian Federal Police spokesperson said authorities were investigating the co-pilot's “links to Australia”. A source briefed on the investigation told Reuters that he had studied at a university in Melbourne.Flydubai has said the circumstances surrounding the incident remain under investigation and that it could not comment further.
Article Summary: Report: Omani co-pilot may have tried to crash aircraft after realising passengers were about to thwart his attempt to seize control of the plane. Corriere della Sera investigation also raised possibility not previously reported, that the co-Pilot may has cut the fuel supply to the aircraft's engines.

Article Title: Flydubai co-pilot 'planned attack before being hired', targeted Israel airport: Reports
Article Text:
Hamam al-Hammami, the accused co-pilot in the flydubai incident (Image source: LinkedIn)

He planned the attack before joining flydubai

What happened on Flight FZ1073

Corriere della Sera

New reports suggest that the flydubai co-pilot accused of attacking his captain and attempting to seize control of a Dubai-to-Tel Aviv flight had planned the attack before he was even hired by the airline. He had also intended to crash the aircraft into Ben Gurion Airport, according to Israeli officials and sources cited in reports.Two Israeli officials with knowledge of the investigation told Reuters that the Omani national, identified as Hamam al-Hammami, told UAE interrogators that he had searched for airlines operating flights to Tel Aviv before applying to flydubai.A third source briefed on the UAE investigation said al-Hammami had previously operated a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv earlier this year and had considered carrying out the attack then. He ultimately abandoned the plan, the source said, because had a friend on board.The latest claims suggest the September 30 incident may have been planned well before al-Hammami joined the airline.Israeli media, citing information from the UAE and Saudi investigations, reported that al-Hammami told investigators he had specifically looked for an airline flying to Tel Aviv before choosing flydubai.“I looked into which airline flies to Tel Aviv. That's why I chose flydubai.I planned it even before I was accepted,” Channel 13 reported him as saying, according to Times of Israel.Times of Israel also reported that al-Hammami had visited Ben Gurion Airport several times in recent months while operating flydubai flights. During a visit in June, he allegedly focused on gathering information and planning an attack, according to the report.He reportedly intended to carry out the attack in July but cancelled it at the last moment because he was friends with one of the crew members.The alleged plan came to a head on September 30, when flydubai Flight FZ1073 was travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv with more than 170 people on board, most of them Israeli passengers.The UAE prosecutor general has described the incident as a “terrorist attack”.Al-Hammami attacked Indian captain Smit Machchhar with an emergency crash axe while the aircraft was over Jordan. According to a timeline reported by Italian newspaper, the co-pilot had requested a prayer break shortly before attacking the captain.Machchhar, despite being wounded, managed to open the cockpit door. An off-duty pilot travelling in the passenger cabin was alerted to the struggle, while passengers rushed into the cockpit and helped subdue al-Hammami.Once his initial plan was disrupted, al-Hammami allegedly tried to crash the aircraft into the desert by forcing the plane into a steep descent and attempting to damage the controls, according to the Italian report.Off-duty pilots on board took over the aircraft and issued an emergency alert. The plane was eventually diverted to Tabuk in northwestern Saudi Arabia, where it landed at 10.57 am.Al-Hammami was detained by Saudi authorities and transferred to the UAE the following day. Machchhar was also taken back to the UAE for medical treatment.The allegations have raised fresh questions about how al-Hammami was allowed to operate a flight to Israel in the first place, as Israel does not have diplomatic relations with Oman and Omani pilots are not permitted to operate flights to Israel.The incident has also exposed questions about earlier warnings concerning al-Hammami, as Oman had previously raised concerns over his online activity and radical views and removed him from flying duties at Oman Air.Israeli and UAE authorities are continuing to investigate the incident. Israeli intelligence officials have been involved in the UAE's questioning of al-Hammami, according to Israeli media reports.A multi-agency Australian counterterrorism unit is also examining his links to Australia, where he studied at RMIT University in Melbourne about a decade ago.
Article Summary: Hamam al-Hammami allegedly planned the attack before joining flydubai. He also intended to crash the aircraft into Ben Gurion Airport, according to reports. The co-pilot is accused of attacking his captain and attempting to seize control of a Dubai-to-Tel Aviv flight.
