Article Title: Russia's pneumonic plague scare: Nearly 200 quarantined after lab worker's death - all you need to know
Article Text:
Nearly 200 people are under observation in Russia after a lab researcher Darya Shipilova died from suspected pneumonic plague.

What Russian authorities have said

Nearly 200 people under observation

Is it pneumonic plague?

US monitoring suspected case

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is most important during a suspected disease outbreak? Quick identification of the infection Monitoring people who may have been exposed Clear and accurate public information Prompt medical treatment and isolation 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Nearly 200 people have been placed under medical observation in Russia's Irkutsk region after a laboratory worker died following severe pneumonia, with reports suggesting she may have contracted plague at a research facility in Siberia. Russian authorities, however, have not publicly confirmed that the woman died from pneumonic plague and have described the illness as a “particularly dangerous infection” and pneumonia of “unknown aetiology”.The case involves an researcher of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute in Shelekhov, near the regional capital Irkutsk, according to Russian state-run news agency TASS and reports cited by CNN.According to reports, the 27 or 28-year-old laboratory worker was admitted to a hospital in Shelekhov on Tuesday with severe pneumonia. She was placed on a ventilator and died on Thursday, according to reports cited by The Moscow Times.Reports said the woman may have accidentally broken a test tube containing live bacteria while collecting samples for testing. The circumstances of the alleged laboratory incident have not been independently confirmed.Russia's federal consumer and health watchdog Rospotrebnadzor said the worker had been diagnosed with “pneumonia of unknown aetiology”, indicating that the exact cause of the illness had not been established.According to CNN, Rospotrebnadzor said “the sanitary and epidemiological situation in the Irkutsk region, the cities of Irkutsk and Shelekhov is stable”.The agency said it had introduced specialised measures “in connection with the case of an employee of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute”.Alexei Tsydenov, head of neighbouring Buryatia, said the woman had died from an unspecified form of plague, according to The Moscow Times. Earlier reports cited by CNN said Tsydenov described the possibility that she had died “possibly from the plague”.At the same time, Tsydenov stressed that “There are no plague outbreaks in the republic, including in areas bordering Mongolia”.Irkutsk governor Igor Kobzev also urged residents to remain calm after an emergency meeting involving regional authorities and Russia's chief state medical officer.According to CNN, Kobzev described the meeting as being linked to a “suspected case of a particularly dangerous infection affecting a resident of the region”.Authorities have stepped up precautionary measures around Shelekhov following the worker's death.According to reports cited by The Moscow Times, at least 197 people who may have come into contact with the woman were placed under medical observation, with more than 100 reportedly in hospital wards.The Shelekhov district hospital was also placed under quarantine while a special commission assessed the situation. Reports also said isolation measures were introduced at at least one maternity facility in the municipality.An aluminium plant located near the research facility instructed employees to wear face coverings.Artem Fominikh, head of the Irkutsk Aluminium Plant, urged people to remain calm amid speculation, saying according to CNN that “there are many rumours and conflicting reports circulating”.“All identified close contacts are under medical supervision. At present, they show no signs of the disease, and their laboratory test results are negative,” Fominikh said, according to CNN.Kobzev similarly said on Telegram that “All identified contact persons have been placed under medical observation. As of today, the contacts show no signs of illness, and their laboratory test results are negative,” according to The Moscow Times.Authorities also reportedly cancelled planned public events in Irkutsk, while law enforcement opened a criminal investigation into possible violations of health and safety rules resulting in death.The exact nature of the infection remains unclear based on the information released publicly by Russian authorities.Media reports have described the case as suspected pneumonic plague, while official statements cited by CNN have referred to pneumonia of unknown origin and a suspected particularly dangerous infection.Gennady Onishchenko, the former head of Rospotrebnadzor, said the pathogen was “most likely not the plague”. He also said that even if plague were confirmed, “there will be no spread of this disease”.Pneumonic plague is one of the three main forms of plague caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. Unlike bubonic plague, which is commonly associated with infected fleas and animals, pneumonic plague affects the lungs and can spread from person to person through respiratory droplets, according to information cited by CNN and the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.Symptoms can include fever, headache and weakness, followed by rapidly developing pneumonia, breathing difficulties, chest pain, coughing and, in some cases, bloody or watery sputum, according to the CDC information cited in the reports.The United States is also monitoring reports of the suspected fatal case, according to a State Department official cited by Fox News.The official said Washington was aware of reports of a death in Irkutsk Oblast and was following the situation in coordination with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and other federal agencies.The official stressed that many details remained unconfirmed and urged Russian authorities to provide accurate information quickly.Former CIA officer Dan Hoffman told Fox News Digital that the US intelligence community was likely collecting information from multiple sources about the incident.“I would also expect our embassy in Moscow to be engaging with their diplomatic counterparts at an official level because we might have people in Russia who might be at risk,” Hoffman said.“Washington will be speaking to all of our allies and partners in the region and sharing what we know.”The State Department official said pneumonic plague can be treated with antibiotics, particularly when treatment begins early, according to Fox News. The CDC recommends starting appropriate treatment as soon as plague is suspected.
Article Summary: Nearly 200 people are under observation in Russia after a lab researcher Darya Shipilova died from suspected pneumonic plague. Reports suggest she may have accidentally broken a test tube containing live bacteria while collecting samples for testing. The circumstances of the alleged laboratory incident have not been independently confirmed. Russian authorities have described the illness as a “particularly dangerous infection” and pneumonia of “unknown aetiology”

Article Title: What drove Gurgaon techie to jump from Noida’s Supernova building: 'Divorce, baby’s premature birth, mounting debts'
Article Text:
Police identified the man as Sambhav Jain, a resident of IMT Manesar who worked for a private company in Gurgaon.

AC mechanic saw him hanging from balcony rails





NOIDA: A 28-year-old software engineer died by suicide after jumping from the balcony of a 41st-floor Airbnb in Supernova in Sector 94 on Saturday morning.A team of AC mechanics working at a nearby flat spotted him hanging from the balcony railing and tried to persuade him to step back. He allegedly told them he was "depressed", before jumping off the edge.Police identified the man as Sambhav Jain, a resident of IMT Manesar who worked for a private company in Gurgaon. He had checked into the Airbnb in Spira tower alone around 3pm on Friday and ordered food online that evening.Two videos of the incident have emerged. One, recorded by a resident of the 17th floor of another tower, shows Jain falling off the balcony. The other, filmed by a member of the AC repair team from a nearby balcony, captures the technicians trying to communicate with him before he jumps."No sooner did we receive information, a team from Sector 126 police station reached the spot and identified the man with the help of ID cards found in his room," said Sumnesh Kumar, SHO of Sector 126.Kumar said Jain had left home around three days ago and stayed at hotels in different places before arriving in Noida. Police are examining WhatsApp conversations between Jain and his father over a monetary dispute"According to the chats, it appeared that his father insisted he return home, but he refused.He said he would repay all the debts first," Kumar said.Police are also examining if personal difficulties, too, may have contributed to his death. The SHO said Jain had married about two years ago, but the relationship ended in a divorce after a few months. Around that time, the couple's baby was born prematurely, and treatment costs reportedly exceeded Rs 30 lakh.Jain, police said, had borrowed money to meet the expenses. At Supernova, a team of police and officials from forensic science laboratory (FSL) inspected the scene and collected evidence. CCTV footage from the building and surrounding areas is being examined too. "An inquest report has been prepared. The body has also been sent for autopsy," Kumar said.
Article Summary: Police identified the man as Sambhav Jain, a resident of IMT Manesar who worked for a private company in Gurgaon. He had checked into the Airbnb in Spira tower alone around 3pm on Friday. Police are examining WhatsApp conversations between Jain and his father over a monetary dispute.

Article Title: ‘Transnational repression’: FBI arrests California woman accused of spying on Taiwan president’s family for China
Article Text:
FBI arrests California woman Wanying Zhang for spying for China, surveilling Taiwan president's son. (Photo Credit: X / @USAttyEssayli)

Taiwan calls alleged surveillance ‘transnational repression’

Why Taiwan's president is a target for Beijing

US-China tensions add to espionage concerns

The FBI has arrested a California woman at Los Angeles International Airport as she was preparing to leave the United States for China, accusing her of acting as an unregistered agent for Beijing and surveilling the family of Taiwan President Lai Ching-te.Wanying Zhang, also known as Heather, 34, was arrested on Sunday and charged with acting as an unregistered foreign agent, according to the FBI and US authorities. Investigators allege that Zhang gathered photographs, videos and vehicle licence plate information about Lai’s son and his family and passed the material to Chinese officials.The arrest comes against the backdrop of intensifying tensions between Beijing and Taipei, with China continuing to claim Taiwan as part of its territory and Lai taking a firm position on the island’s separate political identity.According to the Justice Department, Zhang travelled to Seattle in 2025 at the direction of Chinese officials and subsequently sent them photographs, videos and licence plate information relating to the Taiwanese president’s son and his family.The FBI said Zhang used methods intended to avoid detection while carrying out the alleged surveillance and did not notify US authorities that she was acting on behalf of a foreign government.Bill Essayli, first assistant US attorney for the Central District of California, announced the arrest and said Zhang had been working for China without registering as a foreign agent as required under US law.Zhang was detained at Los Angeles International Airport shortly before she was due to board a flight to China. She is scheduled to appear in federal court in Los Angeles on Monday.It was not immediately clear whether Zhang had an attorney representing her. Her nationality was also not immediately known.Taiwan's Presidential Office confirmed that relatives of Lai were targeted but did not specify whether the president's son was the person under surveillance.Taiwanese officials described the alleged operation as an example of Beijing extending pressure beyond its borders to target people connected to the island's leadership.“This is a classic case of transnational repression,” Presidential Office spokesperson Karen Kuo said in a statement.“Taiwan condemns in the strongest terms such barbaric acts — which disregard human rights and national sovereignty and aim to suppress, threaten, or even harm individuals advocating for freedom and democracy or their families — as such behavior should not be tolerated in the civilized world,” Kuo said.The Chinese Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for comment. China's Foreign Ministry was closed for holidays, according to reports.The Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office in the United States also did not immediately respond to a request for comment.The allegations come as relations between China and Taiwan remain deeply strained.Taiwan and China have been governed separately since the end of a civil war in 1949. Beijing claims sovereignty over the island and has repeatedly threatened to use force if necessary to prevent what it considers a formal separation of Taiwan from China.Lai, who was elected president in 2024, has repeatedly rejected Beijing's sovereignty claims over Taiwan. He has said that Taiwan and China do not belong to each other and that the “People's Republic of China has no right to represent Taiwan.”Beijing considers Lai a separatist and has accused him of being a “destroyer of peace”.Lai's Democratic Progressive Party supports Taiwan's separate political identity, a position that has frequently drawn strong criticism from Beijing.Since taking office, Lai has also sought to strengthen Taiwan's defence capabilities. He has pledged to raise defence spending from 3% to 5% of GDP and has pushed a special budget for construction of the T-Dome air defence system.The arrest also highlights Washington's broader concerns about Chinese intelligence operations and alleged efforts to monitor people connected to Taiwan while they are in the United States.Although the United States does not maintain formal diplomatic relations with Taiwan, Washington is Taipei's most important international supporter and its main source of military equipment.The FBI has not alleged that Zhang was a Chinese government employee, but prosecutors say she acted at the direction of Chinese officials and failed to disclose her relationship with a foreign government.The case is now set to move before a federal court in Los Angeles, where Zhang is expected to face the charges brought against her.
Article Summary: Wanying Zhang, also known as Heather, 34, was arrested on Sunday and charged with acting as an unregistered foreign agent. Investigators allege that Zhang gathered photographs, videos and vehicle licence plate information about Lai’s son and his family and passed the material to Chinese officials.

Article Title: Abducted Kuki farmer found dead with hands tied in Manipur's Kangpokpi
Article Text:
The Kuki Youth Organisation’s Leimakhong block condemned the killing, describing it as a “pre-planned murder” (IANS Photo)





GUWAHATI: The body of a 71-year-old Kuki farmer, Hemjang Haokip, was recovered on Sunday from a remote forest area in Manipur ’s Kangpokpi district with his hands tied, hours after suspected Naga militants allegedly abducted him from his field hut before setting it on fire on Saturday.According to the local village council, Haokip was likely tortured and beaten to death as his body bore injury marks, suggesting that he had been brutally assaulted, sources said.While security forces managed to recover his body, with the aid of sniffer dogs, after Haokip’s clothes were found near his field hut, it was the villagers who brought it out of the forest area in the presence of security personnel.The Kuki Youth Organisation’s Leimakhong block condemned the killing, describing it as a “pre-planned murder”.Alleging involvement of NSCN-IM and Tangkhul elements in Haokip’s killing, the youth organization, in a statement, said, “The circumstances and condition in which he was found is horrifying and have sent shockwaves throughout the Kuki community. The involvement of NSCN-IM and Tangkhul elements in this incident has further intensified the anger and anguish of the community.”The youth body warned that the Kuki community would not remain silent.“We will mobilise every available community mechanism, pursue every avenue, strengthen our collective vigilance, and take every necessary step within our capacity,” it said.On Saturday, the Khunkho Kuki village authority had issued a 24-hour ultimatum to the state authorities and law-enforcement agencies, demanding Haokip’s safe return by Sunday and warning of widespread democratic protests, if he was not found.
Article Summary: The body of a 71-year-old Kuki farmer, Hemjang Haokip, was recovered on Sunday from a remote forest area in Manipur ’s Kangpokpi district with his hands tied. The Kuki Youth Organisation’s Leimakhong block condemned the killing, describing it as a “pre-planned murder”

Article Title: Bengaluru techie drowns in quarry during Instagram-group trek; body found after 2-day search
Article Text:
The deceased, Ganesh Anjaneya Vinay, a resident of Halasuru, belonged to Vijayawada in Andhra Pradesh.

What happened





BENGALURU: A holiday trek, organised through an Instagram group, ended in tragedy after a 30-year-old techie allegedly drowned in a water-filled stone quarry near Yellammanadoddi, close to Jigani, on Oct 2.His body was recovered Sunday morning, following a two-day search operation.The deceased, Ganesh Anjaneya Vinay, a resident of Halasuru, belonged to Vijayawada in Andhra Pradesh.According to the preliminary investigation, Vinay worked as an associate UX designer for a private firm in Bengaluru. Vinay, who had a master’s degree from IIT Delhi, was living in Bengaluru for the past four years.Vinay had joined a group of eight trekkers for the outing during the Gandhi Jayanti holiday weekend. Among those who joined the trek was Vinay’s fiancé, a veterinary doctor.During the outing, the group stopped at a huge stone quarry near Yellammanadoddi. Mining activity at the quarry had reportedly stopped around 15 years ago, and the abandoned pit had since filled with water. The group decided to swim in the quarry.According to police, the group members took a dive and were enjoying themselves when, at around 5.30pm, Vinay suddenly disappeared in the water.The other members tried to rescue him, but were unsuccessful. They alerted Jigani police, who rushed to the spot along with personnel from the fire and emergency services.Police and rescue teams searched the quarry and subsequently summoned personnel from State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), besides involving local divers in the operation.Jigani police later contacted Eshwar Malpe, a scuba diver known for undertaking underwater rescue operations, and his team from Malpe for assistance. After nearly two days of continuous efforts, rescuers finally located Vinay’s body around 9am Sunday.Based on a complaint filed by Vinay’s brother, Jigani police registered an unnatural death report (UDR).The trekking group had connected with each other through Instagram and had planned the trek through the social media group, a senior officer said. The Instagram account regularly shares details about trekking destinations on the outskirts of Bengaluru and in neighbouring districts.According to the members, they had been swimming for around one-and-a-half hours before Vinay drowned.What was meant to be a holiday trek and an adventurous outing ended in tragedy, leaving the group and Vinay’s family traumatised.
Article Summary: Ganesh Anjaneya Vinay, 30, drowned in a water-filled stone quarry near Yellammanadoddi, close to Jigani, on Oct 2. His body was recovered Sunday morning, following a two-day search operation. The trekking group had connected with each other through Instagram and had planned the trek through the social media group.

Article Title: Couple’s 3rd daughter, one-day-old infant strangled inside MP hospital; cops quiz mom, grandma
Article Text:
(Representative image) A one-day-old infant was discovered deceased in the special newborn care unit of Ashoknagar district hospital





BHOPAL: A one-day-old girl, the third daughter of a couple, was allegedly strangled to death inside the special newborn care unit (SNCU) of Ashoknagar district hospital in Madhya Pradesh.The post-mortem report has confirmed murder, and police are questioning the newborn’s mother and grandmother in connection with the case. No arrests had been reported till late Sunday.The baby was born to a couple from a village around 11pm on Friday. She was shifted from the postnatal ward to the SNCU shortly after birth for medical monitoring and care.On Saturday afternoon, the mother noticed marks on the infant’s neck and blood coming from her mouth. She alerted her mother-in-law, following which the baby was taken to a doctor, who declared her dead.Hospital authorities said records showed that only the mother and grandmother had visited the baby inside the SNCU. The grandmother had taken the newborn along to feed her, officials said. The baby’s father had left for the village with his aunt on Saturday morning, while the mother and other family members remained at the hospital.With no CCTV cameras inside the SNCU, police have examined footage from other parts of the hospital to piece together the sequence of events. Police said the circumstances surrounding the death appeared suspicious. A case has been registered, and the mother and grandmother are being questioned as part of the investigation.
Article Summary: A one-day-old girl was allegedly strangled to death inside the special newborn care unit (SNCU) of Ashoknagar district hospital in Madhya Pradesh. Police are questioning the newborn’s mother and grandmother in connection with the case. No arrests had been reported till late Sunday.

Article Title: Telangana woman dies in US after car-truck crash
Article Text:
Daram Supriya, a 31-year-old resident of Telangana, has met with a heartbreaking fate in Missouri, where she died in a road accident.Daram Supriya, a 31-year-old resident of Telangana, has met with a heartbreaking fate in Missouri, where she died in a road accident.





WARANGAL: A 31-year-old woman from Telangana died in a road accident in the St Louis area of Missouri, US, after a truck rammed into her car late on Saturday night. Daram Supriya, a native of Maripeda in Mahabubabad district, was returning home after closing her restaurant when the accident occurred, family members said.While Supriya died on the spot, her friend, who was accompanying her and is from Kodad in Telangana’s Suryapet district, sustained serious injuries. According to reports, the friend was shifted to a nearby hospital, where she is undergoing treatment.“We have no words. We are in a state of shock after learning about the incident,” said D Srinivas, Supriya’s father, who currently lives near Naidupeta Circle in Khammam. He has written to chief minister A Revanth Reddy, urging the govt to help bring his daughter’s mortal remains to India for the last rites. According to him, the accident occurred at around 1.40 am.He said the couple lived in Wentzville, Missouri. While Supriya ran a restaurant, her husband, Kodumuri Ranjith, also from Mahabubabad, works in the software sector. The couple married about five years ago and have a two-and-a-half-year-old son.Both families in Telangana were informed about Supriya’s death by Ranjith.Supriya’s relatives have also sought help from the police and politicians through social media.“Our sister, Daram Supriya, from Khammam met with a car accident in Missouri. We have contacted CP Khammam via WhatsApp. Kindly help us,” read a post from @Harshchoice tagging @INC_Ponguleti and @PonguletiOffice.
Article Summary: Daram Supriya, a 31-year-old resident of Telangana, has met with a heartbreaking fate in Missouri, where she died in a road accident. A truck rammed into her car late on Saturday night. Her friend, who was accompanying her, sustained serious injuries.

Article Title: Protesters climb barricades, confront police in march against CEC Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi; 120 detained
Article Text:
Some clambered onto the barriers and continued shouting slogans as police tried to contain the crowd.





NEW DELHI: Minutes before the march was set to begin, police loudspeakers at India Gate were already telling people to leave. Buses stood ready to carry away detainees, and a heavy deployment guarded the proposed starting point.Within the next few hours, the gathering shifted to Ashoka Road, where hundreds of protesters pushed barricades into the path of a riot-control vehicle, climbed barriers and vehicles, and confronted police trying to block them from Jantar Mantar. Sunday, the third consecutive day of protests against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, saw nearly 120 detentions.At 2.50 pm, police were in force at India Gate. They asked media personnel to keep their identity cards visible. The announcements came a day after three women covering the protests alleged sexual harassment by police personnel.A little after 3 pm, members of AAP and its student wing, ASAP, arrived with other protesters. As they attempted to march, police detained them and took them towards some waiting buses. Some resisted boarding. Others climbed onto a bus and continued chanting. Some protesters broke the rear window of a bus to escape, while some jumped from the moving buses.During the mobilisation, a bus was blocked and detainees freed.For students waiting at India Gate for the march called by All India Students’ Association (AISA) and other Left groups, uncertainty suddenly gave way to a rush towards Ashoka Road.Word spread that the gathering point had shifted to the Andhra Bhawan Circle, and protesters were seen rushing there. Soon, hundreds had assembled. The march stalled at India Gate had found a new gathering point and a fresh line of police to confront.As police arrived in large numbers and a riot-control vehicle approached, the protesters pushed barricades into its path, blocking its movement. Some clambered onto the barriers and continued shouting slogans as police tried to contain the crowd. The barricades became the centre of a face-off.Around 5 pm, the confrontation shifted to a vehicle near Shangri-La hotel, where AISA president Neha Bora was taken, according to a complaint the organisation sent the Delhi Police commissioner. Women protesters tried to climb onto the vehicle, while women police personnel struggled to pull them away. Bora reportedly also scaled a barricade. Protesters later marched towards the Windsor Place roundabout too. Traffic was severely affected around the area.Apart from the common cause of demanding Kumar’s resignation, for some in the crowd, anger over police’s way of handling of the protests was another reason to turn up. “Even if prohibitory orders have been imposed, we want to march,” said Mannat, an artist. “When police themselves are attacking women, don’t the rules apply to them?”Women from various colleges said they had joined the marches demanding safer public spaces. Their concerns about women’s safety now extended to the treatment of protesters and journalists. Suhana, a participant, said she had returned because of what she described as police brutality Saturday. She alleged that she had been detained at 1.30 pm. “I was touched inappropriately by police personnel. Police acknowledged my written complaint with a stamp, but neither registered an FIR, nor arranged for a medical examination,” she said.In its complaint, AISA alleged that male police personnel without badges had taken Bora away in a vehicle. No woman police officer was there. The organisation described this as an “abduction”. An AISA member later said Bora was released in the Narela industrial area police station but did not have her phone or bag.Police had said permission had not been granted for the marches.Later in the day, Indian Youth Congress workers marched from Raisina Road towards Jantar Mantar. They demanded Kumar’s resignation and accused Centre of protecting him.
Article Summary: Third consecutive day of protests against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar saw nearly 120 detentions. Protesters pushed barricades into the path of a riot-control vehicle, climbed barriers and vehicles, and confronted police trying to block them from Jantar Mantar.

Article Title: Punjab cop whose brother was murdered earlier shot at by bike-borne men near Amritsar home; police suspect old family feud
Article Text:
Sukhchain Singh, a Government Railway Police personnel, was injured in a shooting incident by unidentified assailants.





AMRITSAR: A Government Railway Police (GRP) personnel was injured after three unidentified bike-borne assailants allegedly opened fire at him near Ajnala in Punjab’s Amritsar district on Sunday evening, police said.The injured personnel, identified as Sukhchain Singh, a resident of Jagdev Khurd village, is posted at Amritsar Railway Station. The incident occurred near a canal, around one kilometre from his home, while he was returning from duty on his motorcycle in plain clothes.According to police, one of the bullets hit Singh’s left shoulder and passed through. He was rushed to Civil Hospital, where he is undergoing treatment and is stated to be out of danger.Deputy Superintendent of Police Dharminder Kalyan said an FIR has been registered and the police are investigating the incident from all angles.Singh said three men riding a motorcycle approached him from behind, fired at him and fled. As his home was nearby, he managed to reach there before being taken for medical treatment.The GRP personnel also suspected that the shooting could be linked to an old family dispute, claiming that his brother had earlier been murdered. He said the attackers may have known his identity despite him being in plain clothes.Police teams are scanning CCTV footage from the area to identify the assailants and establish the motive behind the attack. Further action will be taken based on the findings of the investigation.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: A Government Railway Police (GRP) personnel was injured after three unidentified bike-borne assailants allegedly opened fire at him. The injured personnel, identified as Sukhchain Singh, a resident of Jagdev Khurd village, is posted at Amritsar Railway Station. The incident occurred near a canal, around one kilometre from his home, while he was returning from duty.

Article Title: ‘Govt planning to arrest Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka’: CJP’s Saurav Das calls for biggest mobilisation from Oct 10
Article Text:
“The protests must continue. People of India should ensure the biggest mobilisation starting October 10th,” Das said.

(With agency inputs)





NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) chief spokesperson Saurav Das claimed that the government was planning to arrest him and several other party leaders, including Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Ratna Singh, and called for the biggest mobilisation of protesters from October 10.In a post on X, Das alleged that the government believed such actions would suppress the movement, but said the “young generation has awakened”. He appealed to people to continue protesting for their rights and future, “with or without us”.“The protests must continue. People of India should ensure the biggest mobilisation starting October 10th,” Das said.Das also said CJP leaders were prepared to face arrest or worse, but warned that any such action by the government would be a “big mistake”.“If the government thinks that such dictatorial actions will work, then they are mistaken. The young will not tolerate this,” he said."The government is planning on arresting me, Abhijeet, Ashutosh, Ratna and other Cockroach Janta Party leaders,” Das tweeted.The post came hours after protests were held outside Parliament Street police station on Sunday following allegations by a woman journalist that Delhi Police personnel had molested and sexually assaulted her during a protest.Das, who was at the police station along with CJP legal team lead Ratna Singh, the complainant and her lawyers, demanded that police register an FIR in the case.He questioned the police for not meeting the protesters, saying they had been waiting for a response from the authorities.“The complainant, the victim, is here, along with her lawyers and the rest of us. Why won’t they speak to us? We have given them two or three minutes; otherwise, we are going to storm inside,” Das told news agency ANI while addressing protesters outside the police station.Das said he and Singh had gone to the Parliament Street police station to support the woman and alleged that Delhi Police had not cooperated with her.“Today, on behalf of the 'Cockroach Janata Party,' Ratna Singh and I have come to the Parliament Street Police Station to support the victim,” he said.He also accused police of detaining, assaulting and manhandling young protesters during the ongoing demonstrations and referred to the violence witnessed during the July 20 protest.“The Delhi Police should be ashamed of their attitude—especially after the brutality seen on July 20th; this is how they are behaving,” Das said.
Article Summary: “The protests must continue. People of India should ensure the biggest mobilisation starting October 10th,” Das said. CJP leaders were prepared to face arrest or worse, but warned that any such action by the government would be a “big mistake”

Article Title: Mankind Pharma to give Rs 1 crore to Flydubai hero Capt Smit Machchhar, family
Article Text:
Mankind Pharma has granted Rs 1 crore to Capt Smit Machchhar, recognizing his heroic actions during a tumultuous incident while piloting flydubai flight FZ1073

Smit Machchhar's actions during mid-air crisis

Pilots' body seeks national bravery award





MUMBAI: Mankind Pharma has announced Rs 1 crore in financial support for flydubai pilot Capt Smit Machchhar and his family, recognising his "extraordinary courage, composure and sense of responsibility demonstrated during a moment of unprecedented crisis. "Machchhar has been widely praised after a dramatic mid-air incident on September 30, when flydubai flight FZ1073, carrying 174 passengers and eight crew members, came under attack inside the cockpit during its Dubai-Tel Aviv journey. The first officer allegedly attacked Machchhar, leaving him seriously injured.Despite his injuries, Machchhar continued to discharge his responsibilities as pilot-in-command and helped ensure the aircraft was brought under control before it was diverted safely to Tabuk in Saudi Arabia, the Federation of Indian Pilots said.Machchhar, despite being seriously injured, managed to activate the cockpit door release, allowing passengers and crew members to enter and overpower the attacker. The aircraft had also undergone a rapid descent during the incident before it was stabilised.The flight was carrying 174 passengers and eight crew members when the incident occurred, according to the Federation of Indian Pilots.Machchhar later told Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a video call that he had been reciting the Hanuman Chalisa during the ordeal to remain composed.Modi praised him for his courage and presence of mind.The Federation of Indian Pilots has also written to the Prime Minister seeking a national bravery award or another appropriate civilian honour for Machchhar, citing his conduct during the emergency.The pilots' body said his decision to continue performing his duties despite being injured demonstrated exceptional courage and responsibility towards the passengers and crew.Machchhar's family and residents in Mumbai had earlier spoken about their relief after the aircraft landed safely, while people gathered outside his Tilak Nagar home to honour him and seek a gallantry award.Mankind Pharma's announcement adds to the recognition being extended to the pilot following the mid-air crisis.
Article Summary: Mankind Pharma has granted Rs 1 crore to Capt Smit Machchhar, recognizing his heroic actions during a tumultuous incident while piloting flydubai flight FZ1073. Federation of Indian Pilots has also written to the Prime Minister seeking a national bravery award or another appropriate civilian honour.

Article Title: Gangotri National Park entry suspended after heavy rain, snowfall; routes to reopen in 2-3 days
Article Text:
The park is expected to reopen to tourists and trekkers within two to three days once all routes are restored.





UTTARKASHI: Following heavy rainfall and snowfall in the high-altitude Himalayan region on September 26 and 27, the Gangotri National Park administration has suspended entry into the park area until further orders, citing the safety of tourists and trekkers.Mayank Garg, Deputy Director of Gangotri National Park, told TOI that the heavy rain and snow have made various trekking routes within the park—including Gangotri-Gaumukh-Tapovan, Gartang Gali, and Kedartal—hazardous; the paths have sustained damage in several places and are currently being repaired.The park is expected to reopen to tourists and trekkers within two to three days once all routes are restored.Entry into the park area will remain prohibited until further notice to ensure the safety of tourists and trekkers.Meanwhile, Manoj Rawat, Secretary of the Uttarkashi Trekking Association, expressed concern over the sudden closure of trekking routes.He noted that tourists are facing inconvenience, as many have made advance bookings, and trekking companies have already arranged for rations, equipment, and other essential supplies.He argued that the park administration should not impose restrictions on the safer, easier routes.
Article Summary: Following heavy rainfall and snowfall in the high-altitude Himalayan region, the Gangotri National Park administration has suspended entry into the park area. The park is expected to reopen to tourists and trekkers within two to three days once all routes are restored.

Article Title: ‘Deep cut on neck’: Squabble over a book, teen slashes classmate in south Kolkata school
Article Text:
A boy whipped out a sharp object and attacked a classmate, who started bleeding profusely, triggering panic among the students (AI Imgae)

(Written with inputs from Dwaipayan Ghosh & Sumati Yengkhom in Kolkata)





KOLKATA: A 15-year-old Class IX student of a prominent south Kolkata school ended in hospital and underwent surgery after being slashed with a sharp object by a classmate inside the classroom during school hours on Wednesday.The injured teenager sustained deep cuts on his neck and multiple fingers of the left hand.According to a statement issued by the school, the incident took place around 12.29 pm in the presence of the class teacher while the class was in progress.A boy whipped out a sharp object and attacked a classmate, who started bleeding profusely, triggering panic among the students. Teachers immediately took the injured boy to the school infirmary, where nurses administered first aid before senior staff members took him to Ruby General Hospital and informed his parents.The boy who committed the assault was taken away from the classroom and counselled by school psychologists. Later, his father took him home. The school also filed a report with Gariahat police station.Additional Police Commissioner (crime) Kunal Agarwal said, “We have received a complaint from the school and are registering a case under appropriate sections of law. We have learned from the school authorities that the victim is now stable, and that the accused is an autistic child.”Ruby General Hospital said in a statement that the 15-year-old boy was first admitted to the hospital emergency. “After initial examination and resuscitation, he was taken to the OT. There was a deep laceration on the neck extending up to the face, with underlying muscle injury. Also, there was an extensor tendon injury of the left index finger along with cuts on multiple other fingers,” the statement said. “All the injuries were repaired and the patient is presently stable,” the hospital said after the surgery. The student is being treated by plastic and reconstructive surgeon Dipanjan Dey.According to teachers, the immediate trigger of the incident appears to be a squabble between the two boys over a book on Tuesday, which ended with the book getting torn. Some claimed the squabble had turned physical on Tuesday as well, but the teachers separated the two and ensured that both were counselled.After the surgery, the victim’s father told TOI, “I have not spoken to my son yet. When we dashed to the hospital, we saw a deep wound in the neck. He has been in this school since childhood. My younger child also studies in this school. He did not tell us about about any incident in school yesterday. He is usually very quiet. We are still processing this.”South Point High School in a statement said, “The incident has caused considerable distress and shock among the pupils, teachers, staff, and the wider school community. The school is deeply concerned about the physical and emotional well-being of everyone affected by the incident, particularly the children who witnessed or were otherwise impacted by what happened.”The statement added, “The school will take all necessary steps to address the emotional and psychological impact of the incident. The school remains committed to ensuring a safe, caring, and supportive environment for all its pupils and staff while dealing with the aftermath of this unfortunate incident.”A senior school official, who requested anonymity, said, “We will investigate and take not only corrective action but preventive action as well.”
Article Summary: A 15-year-old Class IX student of a prominent south Kolkata school ended in hospital and underwent surgery after being slashed with a sharp object by a classmate. The injured teenager sustained deep cuts on his neck and multiple fingers of the left hand. The boy who committed the assault was taken away from the classroom and counselled by school psychologists.

Article Title: Over 100 hearings, 22 witnesses: Wife, lover convicted in Meerut ‘blue drum’ murder case; sentencing on Oct 14
Article Text:
The verdict came after more than 100 hearings and examination of 22 witnesses





MEERUT: A district and sessions court in Meerut on Wednesday convicted Muskan Rastogi and her lover Sahil Shukla of murdering Muskan’s husband, merchant navy officer Saurabh Rajput, dismembering his body and concealing it in a blue plastic drum filled with cement in March 2025.The verdict came after more than 100 hearings and examination of 22 witnesses, with the court fixing Oct 14 for the pronouncement of the sentence.Prosecution lawyer K K Chaubey said district and sessions judge Arvind Kumar Mishra found both accused guilty of murder and destruction of evidence. Muskan and Sahil appeared before the court through video conferencing. “The court observed that the crime falls into a category that not only shreds the fabric of society but also strikes at the foundation of the husband-wife relationship,” Chaubey said. He added that when the court asked the two to make submissions on the sentence, they said they had nothing to say.Rajput’s mother, Renu Devi , was present at the court when the verdict was pronounced. “We have waited for this day for the last 18 months. We want nothing less than capital punishment for both,” she said.The case dated back to March 2025, when Muskan and Sahil killed Rajput, chopped his body into pieces, and placed the remains in a blue plastic drum filled with cement in an attempt to conceal the crime.The case came to light on March 17 after a foul smell began emanating from the drum, leading to the discovery of the body and subsequent investigation.Muskan and Sahil were arrested following the discovery and remained in custody during the trial. The gruesome manner in which Rajput’s body was concealed led to the case becoming widely known as the “blue drum murder case”. The court will hear the matter on sentencing on Oct 14.Feb 24-25, 2025: Saurabh Rajput returns to Meerut from London; Muskan’s birthday celebrated next dayMarch 4: Muskan, Sahil drug Saurabh, stab him to death, dismember body; remains packed in blue drum with cement; duo leaves for Himachal PradeshMid-March: Muskan tells maternal family about murder; police case follows; remains recovered from drum on Mar 17March 18, 2025: Muskan, Sahil arrestedMarch 19, 2025: Court sends duo to 14-day judicial custodyMay 12, 2025: Police file nearly 1,000-page chargesheet; around 34 witness statements; murder, destruction-of-evidence chargesNov 24, 2025: Muskan gives birth to girl while in custody; mother, newborn shifted to women’s barrack; Saurabh’s family seeks DNA test for paternityMar 2025-Sept 2026: Trial spans around 13 months; 22 witnesses examinedSept 17, 2026: Final arguments conclude; prosecution seeks death penalty for bothSept 30: Muskan, Sahil convicted of murder, destruction of evidence; sentencing fixed for Oct 14
Article Summary: The verdict came after more than 100 hearings and examination of 22 witnesses. The court will hear the matter on sentencing on Oct 14. The gruesome manner in which Rajput’s body was concealed led to the case becoming widely known as the ‘blue drum murder case’

Article Title: ‘I agree’: CJP's Abhijeet Dipke backs post calling Neha Bora ‘more talented’ than him
Article Text:
Neha Bora, a prominent figure in the All India Students' Association, shared a humorous moment with Abhijeet Dipke

Who is Neha Bora?

Dipke announces October 10 Jantar Mantar protest

CJP, AISA activists among protesters





NEW DELHI: A social media post comparing student leader Neha Bora with Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke prompted a light-hearted exchange between the two on X, after a user called Bora "more talented" and described her as a "complete Gen Z icon". Dipke responded simply: "I agree."The X user had posted: "Maturity is realizing Neha Bora is more talented than Abhijeet Dipke. A complete Gen Z icon with an absolutely ridiculous aura."Dipke replied to the post with: "I agree."Another user responded to Dipke's reply, writing: "Only legends can appreciate each other.."Neha Bora is the national president of the All India Students' Association (AISA) and has been involved in the ongoing protests over electoral-roll revision and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Bora was among those detained during the October 2 protest in Delhi and later urged protesters to return to Jantar Mantar and continue their demonstration.Dipke, the founder of the CJP, has been leading the party's campaign seeking Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.The CJP held a large protest at Mumbai's Shivaji Park on Friday, following which Dipke announced another demonstration at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on October 10 if Kumar does not resign.Dipke said the October 10 protest would be peaceful and called on people who want free and fair elections to join the agitation.The latest protests have brought together student and youth activists in Delhi, with hundreds detained after demonstrators attempted to reach Jantar Mantar on October 2. AISA's Bora was among those detainedThe exchange between Bora and Dipke, meanwhile, added a lighter social-media moment to the continuing political mobilisation around the protests.
Article Summary: Neha Bora is the national president of the All India Students' Association (AISA) She has been involved in the ongoing protests over electoral-roll revision and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. A social media post comparing Bora with Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke prompted a light-hearted exchange.
